# Key Variables in Procurement Processing Data

```{r procurement_dataset, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(911)

          "Akosua" ,"Adjoa" ,"Abena" ,"Akua" ,"Yaa" ,"Efia" ,"Ama")

date_to = as.Date("2026-09-28")
```

# 1. product details
```{r }
product_details = rbind(data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "agriculture" ,
                                   product_name = product_goods_agric ) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "miscellaneous" ,
                                   product_name  = product_goods_misc) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "office supplies" ,
                                   product_name  = product_goods_office) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "services" ,
                                   product_category = "service" ,
                                   product_name  = product_services)  ) %>%
  mutate(product_id = sprintf("PROD%03d" ,1:39) ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:4) ,as.factor) ,
         freq = 1)
```

# 2. Price range of Product
```{r }
# Average Prices in Ghana (2026) with Product IDs

set.seed(911)
price_list = data.frame(product_id = sprintf("PROD%03d" ,1:39) ,
                        price_range = price_range) %>%

left_join(data.frame(product_id = product_details[,4],
                     product_name = product_details[,3] ) )  %>%
  
  separate(price_range, into = c("min_price", "max_price"), sep = "-") %>%
  mutate(min_price = as.numeric(min_price),
         max_price = as.numeric(max_price) ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(price1 = round(runif(1, min_price ,max_price ) ,2),
         price2 = round(runif(1, min_price ,max_price ) ,2),
         price3 = round(runif(1, min_price ,max_price ) ,2) ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  pivot_longer(c(2,3,5,6,7) ,
               names_to = "price_type" ,
               values_to = "price") %>%
  select(-price_type) %>%
  mutate(price_id = sprintf("PRID%003d" ,1:195) ,
         price = round(price ,2) ,
         freq = 1) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1,2,4) ,as.factor))

#write_csv(price_list ,
#          "C:/Users/broda/Documents/data insights/Leo -HRpc/09 Bunge/data/z_price_list.csv")

summary(price_list)
hist(price_list$price)

price_list %>%
  group_by(product_name) %>%
  summarise(avg_price = mean(price))

```

# 5. Purchase Requisition
```{r }
set.seed(123)
product_request = supplier_price_list %>%
  slice(rep(1:n() ,length.out=3000))

purchase_requisition = data.frame(pr_number = sprintf("PR%04d" ,1:3000) ,
                                  requester = paste(sample(fname ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
                                                    sample(lname ,3000 ,replace = TRUE)) ,
                                  department = sample(department ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
                                  product_type = product_request[,11]   ,
                                  product_category = product_request[,12]  ,
                                  product_name = product_request[,13]  ,
                                  product_id = product_request[,2]  ,
                                  description = "" ,
                                  UoM = as.factor("") ,
                                  quantity = round(rnorm(3000 ,400 ,100) ,0)  ,
                                  unit_price = product_request[,14] ,
                                  prefered_supplier = product_request[,1] ,
                                  date_requested = sample(date ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) - 30 ) %>%
  mutate(quantity = ifelse(product_category == "service" ,round(quantity/100,0) ,round(quantity/10,0)) ,
         date_expected = date_requested + round(rnorm(3000 ,45 ,10) ,0) ,
         contact = paste0(requester ,"@yenwho.com") ,
         pr_approval = sample(c("yes" ,"no") ,prob = c(0.9 ,0.1) ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
         freq = 1 ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:4,7,8,15,16) ,as.factor))

write_csv(purchase_requisition ,
          "C:/Users/broda/Documents/data insights/Leo -HRpc/09 Bunge/data/z_purchase_requisition.csv") 

# chk for NA
 summary(purchase_requisition )

```

# 6. Purchase Order after approval of request
```{r }
set.seed(911)
len_po = length(purchase_requisition$pr_approval[purchase_requisition$pr_approval == "yes"])

purchase_order = purchase_requisition %>%
  filter(pr_approval == "yes") %>%
  mutate(total_price = unit_price * quantity ,
         #invoiced = sample(c("yes" ,"no") ,prob = c(0.95 ,0.05) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         PO_number = as.factor(paste0(year(date_requested) ,"-" ,sprintf("%05d" ,seq(c(1:len_po))))) ,
         date_order = date_requested + sample(7:14 ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         eta = sample(delivery_eta ,prob = c(0.6 ,0.2 ,0.15 ,0.05) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         cycling_time = round(rnorm(len_po ,110 ,30) ,0) ,
           #sample(delivery_otd ,prob = c(0.4, rep(0.6/17, 17)) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         supplier_ID = prefered_supplier ,
         status = as.factor(sample(c("sent" ,"pending") ,len_po ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.95 ,0.05))) ) %>%
  mutate(status = as.factor(ifelse(status == "sent" & product_name == "research" ,"pending" ,
                                   paste(status))) ,
         date_order = case_when(status == "sent" ~ date_order ,status == "pending" ~ as.Date(0)) ,
         eta = as.numeric(ifelse(status == "sent" ,eta ,"")) ,
         cycling_time = as.numeric(ifelse(eta == 30 ,round(rnorm(1000 ,30 ,5) ,0) ,
                                          ifelse(status == "sent" ,cycling_time ,""))) )%>%
  mutate(total_price = as.numeric(ifelse(status == "sent" ,unit_price * quantity ,"")) ) %>%
  select(-c(2:5, 14:15))

write_csv(purchase_order ,
          "C:/Users/broda/Documents/data insights/Leo -HRpc/09 Bunge/data/z_purchase_order.csv")

 summary( purchase_order %>% 
            group_by(eta ,cycling_time ) %>%
            summarise(tp = sum(total_price)) )

```

```{r }
set.seed(911)
len_invoice = length(purchase_order$status[purchase_order$status == "sent"])

invoice = suppliers %>%
  select(supplier_ID ,supplier_name ,bank_info) %>%
  
  left_join(

         otd = sample(seq(20, 190, by = 10) ,len_invoice ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.4, rep(0.6/17, 17))) )         ,by = c("supplier_ID" = "prefered_supplier") ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="") ) %>%
  mutate(invoice_no = paste0(word(supplier_name ,2) ,"-" ,invoice_no) ) %>%
```

# 8. supplier analysis
```{r }
set.seed(911)
len_sup = nrow(purchase_order)


supplier_analysis = suppliers %>%
  mutate(risk = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.35 ,0.30 ,0.20 ,0.10 ,0.05) ) ,
         impact = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.10 ,0.10 ,0.30 ,0.20 ,0.30) ) ,
         psat = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.10,0.10,0.2,0.3,0.3))  ,
         csat = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.15,0.15,0.1,0.3,0.3)) ,
          nps = sample(0:10 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,
                        prob = c(0.04,0.04, 0.04, 0.04, 0.04, 0.04 ,0.04,
                                 0.21 ,0.11 ,
                                 0.20 ,0.20))  ) %>%
  mutate(nps_cat = ifelse(nps > 8 ,"promoter" ,ifelse(nps < 7 ,"detractor" ,
                   ifelse(nps %in% c(7,8) ,"passive" ,nps))) ,
         psat_cat = ifelse(psat > 3,"high" ,ifelse(psat < 3,"low" ,ifelse(psat == 3,"medium" ,psat))) ,
         csat_cat = ifelse(csat > 3,"high" ,ifelse(csat < 3,"low" ,ifelse(csat == 3,"medium" ,csat))) ,
         risk_level = ifelse(risk > 3,"high" ,ifelse(risk < 3,"low" ,ifelse(risk == 3,"medium" ,csat))) ,
         impact_level = ifelse(impact > 3,"high" ,ifelse(impact < 3,"low" ,
                      ifelse(impact == 3,"medium" ,csat)))) %>%
  
  right_join(purchase_order) %>%
  left_join(product_details ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="") ) %>%
  
  mutate(status_delivery = ifelse(eta >= cycling_time ,"on-time" ,"delayed") ,
         defects = ifelse(status == "sent" & product_type == "goods" ,
                          sample(c("no" ,"yes") ,len_sup ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.8,0.2)) ,"" )) %>%
  mutate(across(c(15:19,24,29,38,39) ,as.factor))

write_csv(supplier_analysis ,
          "C:/Users/broda/Documents/data insights/Leo -HRpc/09 Bunge/data/y_supplier_analysis.csv")

summary(supplier_analysis %>%
          group_by(eta ,cycling_time ,status_delivery) %>%
          summarise(tp = sum(total_price)))

```
# 9 .Predictive Analytics

## 9a. random forest
```{r }
set.seed(911)
supplier_prediction = na.omit(supplier_analysis)

split = sample(1:nrow(supplier_prediction) ,0.7*nrow(supplier_prediction))
train_data = supplier_prediction[split ,]
test_data = supplier_prediction[-split ,]

rf_model = randomForest(risk_level ~ supplier_origin +supplier_category +classification +nps_cat
                        +psat_cat +csat_cat +product_category  ,
                        data = train_data ,
                        ntree = 500 ,      # number of trees
                        mtry = 3 ,          # number of variables per split
                        importance = TRUE)

rf_model

```

### model evaluation & variable importance
```{r }
predictions = predict(rf_model, test_data)
confusion_matrix = table(test_data$cycling_time, predictions)
confusion_matrix

accuracy = sum(diag(confusion_matrix)) / sum(confusion_matrix)
accuracy

# variable importance
importance(rf_model)
varImpPlot(rf_model)

```

## 9b. rpart
```{r }
set.seed(911)
tree_model = rpart(risk_level ~ supplier_category +classification +product_category ,
                   #supplier_origin +nps_cat +psat_cat +csat_cat +  ,
                    data = train_data ,method = "class" )

print(tree_model)
summary(tree_model)
rpart.plot(tree_model)

predictions = predict(tree_model ,test_data ,type = "class")

cm = confusionMatrix(predictions ,test_data$risk_level)

print(cm)

accuracy = cm$overall["Accuracy"]
print(accuracy)



bestcp = tree_model$cptable[which.min(tree_model$cptable[, "xerror"]) ,"CP"]

pruned_tree = prune(tree_model ,cp = bestcp)

rpart.plot(pruned_tree)

pruned_pred = predict(pruned_tree ,test_data ,type = "class")

confusionMatrix(pruned_pred ,test_data$risk_level)

```


# tree package
```{r }
set.seed(123)

# Fit tree
tree_fit = tree(risk_level ~ supplier_origin +supplier_category +classification 
                +nps_cat +psat_cat +csat_cat +product_category  ,
                data = train_data)

# Plot
plot(tree_fit)
text(tree_fit, pretty = 0)

# Cross-validation
cv_fit = cv.tree(tree_fit ,FUN = prune.misclass)

# Select best size
best_size = cv_fit$size[which.min(cv_fit$dev)]

# Prune
pruned_tree = prune.misclass(tree_fit ,best = best_size)

# Predict
pred = predict(pruned_tree ,newdata = test_data ,type = "class")

# Validate
confusionMatrix(pred ,test_data$risk_level)

```

Supplier classification categorizes vendors by criticality, risk, and strategic value to optimize procurement, typically splitting them into strategic/core, preferred, tactical, and nuisance categories. Organizations use these classifications to focus management efforts, with common types including Tier 1-3, ESG, and diversity statuses.

Common Supplier Classification List
Strategic/Core Supplier: High-value, long-term partners essential for competitive advantage.
Preferred Supplier: Proven vendors with high performance, prioritized for new business.
Tactical/Operational Supplier: Suppliers of standard, low-risk items with many alternatives.
Bottleneck Supplier: Low spend but high risk if supply fails (e.g., sole source).
Nuisance/Divest Supplier: High-cost, low-value vendors to be phased out.

Classification FrameworksTier Levels (Supply Chain):
Tier 1: Direct suppliers of final products/services.
Tier 2: Suppliers to Tier 1.
Tier 3: Suppliers to Tier 2 (often raw materials).

Supplier Characteristics:
Diversity Owned: Woman, minority, or veteran-owned.
ESG Compliant: Meets Environmental, Social, and Governance standards.
Certified: Holds specific ISO, FDA, or OSHA certifications.

Examples of Classification Types
High-Volume: Providers of critical consumables like fuel or electricity.
Non-Substitutable: Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs).

Risk Level: Low, Medium, or High (based on financial or geopolitical factors).
